assessments.zone: Nyanga and Kitangwa secteurs / health zones (rural west and north-west of Tshikapa towards the Kwilu/Loange and the Angolan border: Mbangu, Mukundsu, Nyanga, Mundu, Kungu, Kabunda, etc.)
assessments.evidence: Rural Pende/Tshokwe areas with no reported armed-group activity in recent years; state presence via PNC posts at secteur/groupement centres, FARDC/DGM along the Angolan border, and customary chiefs handling day-to-day disputes.

assessments.zone: Peri-urban and rural localities of Tshikapa health zone around the city (Kamikula/Ngombe, Muyeji, Kashimba, Matshibola, Kabudila, Kapakasa, Mbambi Kakondo, etc.)
assessments.evidence: Villages and diamond-digging settlements adjoining Tshikapa city along the Kasai/Tshikapa rivers; no reported armed-group activity in recent years. State security (PNC posts, FARDC nearby in Tshikapa) with customary chiefs handling local disputes.

assessments.zone: Mutena secteur / Mutena health zone (artisanal diamond fields east of Tshikapa: Mutena mission, Tshiabindu, Mutshima, Kamabanji, Lubanga, Tshisenge, etc.)
assessments.evidence: Large artisanal diamond-mining settlements with police (incl. mines police) posts and some FARDC presence at mining sites, where security forces are frequently reported to tax/extort diggers. The area was affected by Kamuina Nsapu violence in 2017 but no active armed-group control is known since 2018.

assessments.zone: Tshikapa city neighbourhoods (health areas Katshongo, Kabuatu, Kibulungu, La Paix, Tshisele, Bel'Air, Tite, Bakuba, Tshitangu, Kasanji, Kizito, Kalupombi, Masangu, Kabikabi) – provincial capital of Kasaï
assessments.evidence: Tshikapa is the seat of Kasaï provincial institutions with a permanent PNC provincial commissariat, FARDC garrison and ANR. No armed group has held the city since the 2017 Kamuina Nsapu crisis (which hit Kamonia/Tshikapa outskirts but was suppressed in 2017-2018); insecurity is limited to urban banditry and occasional community tensions handled by police.

assessments.zone: Tshikapa city (provincial capital of Kasaï) and its neighbourhoods/health areas
assessments.evidence: Provincial capital with permanent PNC commissariats, FARDC garrison and ANR; no armed group has held any part of Tshikapa since the 2017 Kamuina Nsapu attacks were repulsed. Urban banditry exists but does not displace police control. Not verified with fresh sources in this run (web research unavailable).

assessments.zone: Rural Kamonia territory part 1: secteurs Kanzala, Kamonia, Kamwesha, Kalonda Ouest (towns such as Kawazanga, Kabambi Nkonko, Kayanda, Kasanzu, Tshikubu, Kotshi)
assessments.evidence: Former Kamuina Nsapu theatre (2016-2017) where militias were dispersed or demobilised by 2018-2019; since then no armed group is known to control territory, and order is maintained by PNC posts with customary chiefs and FARDC deployments (incl. along the Angolan border and diamond-mining areas). Sporadic residual militia or intercommunal incidents possible but not known to amount to control. Not verified with fresh sources in this run.

230.title: Report of the Team of International Experts on the situation in the Kasai regions (A/HRC/38/31)

units.CD9202-kamonia-2: Eastern part of Kamonia territory plus Tshikapa city (Kasaï). Since the Kamuina Nsapu insurgency was suppressed in 2017-2018 there is no known armed-group control in Tshikapa, Mutena, Nyanga or Kitangwa; the state holds the area, with the PNC as the everyday security force and FARDC garrisons in Tshikapa and at diamond-mining sites. Main insecurity is urban banditry in Tshikapa, security-force extortion in the Mutena diamond fields and occasional intercommunal tensions. Assessment relies on background knowledge because live web research was unavailable (search quota exhausted, news sites blocked), so confidence is medium for the city and low for rural areas.
units.CD9202-kamonia-1: Northern/central Kamonia territory (Kasaï) including the provincial capital Tshikapa and the secteurs of Kanzala, Kamonia, Kamwesha and Kalonda Ouest. The Kamuina Nsapu insurgency that hit Kamonia (Kamako, Kamwesha, Kamonia secteurs) in 2016-2017 was defeated/demobilised by 2018-2019 and only sporadic residual militia incidents and intercommunal (Pende/Tshokwe vs Luba/Lulua) tensions have been reported since. No armed group is known to hold territory in the unit as of 2026; Tshikapa is policed by the PNC with FARDC (21st military region units) and ANR present, and rural secteurs fall under PNC posts and customary chiefs. Assessment relies on background knowledge because live web research was unavailable in this run, so confidence is limited.
